c.tagline: Sugar-cane hills meet a historic Caribbean harbor town.

taxi.fareNote: Rates are set by the St. Kitts Taxi Association by origin/destination zone; agree the fare with the driver before departure since meters aren't used.

emergency.note: 911 reaches police, fire, and ambulance islandwide; Joseph N. France General Hospital in Basseterre is the main public hospital.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Avoid the McKnight and Newtown neighborhoods after dark, where most of the island's gang-related violence occurs.
Petty theft spikes around Port Zante on cruise-ship days, and unlit streets outside the center are best avoided at night — take taxis.

hood_desc: Colonial-era streets around the clock-tower Circus and Independence Square, next to the Port Zante cruise pier; best for first-timers who want historic sights, duty-free shopping, and budget stays within walking distance of everything.

A narrow isthmus south of downtown lined with beach bars, a casino resort, and a golf course, split between a calm Caribbean-side beach and a livelier Atlantic strip; suits travelers who want nightlife and beach access close to town.

A quieter, upscale stretch of white-sand bays like Cockleshell and Turtle Beach with a marina and golf course; suits honeymooners and travelers seeking seclusion who don't mind a 20-30 minute drive from town.
A hillside residential district just west of downtown with harbor views and long-established hotels; suits travelers who want an easy walk or short drive into Basseterre with a quieter, local feel.

Historic sugar-plantation inns and eco-luxury lodges set among rainforest and old cane fields on the island's quieter north side; suits travelers wanting nature and a slower pace, with a rental car recommended.
lodging: St. Kitts Marriott Resort & The Royal Beach Casino
Koi Resort Saint Kitts, Curio Collection by Hilton

water.note: Tap water is treated and chlorinated and officially considered safe to drink.

sys.n: St. Kitts private route buses (green 'H'/'HA' plates)

transit.pay: Bus fares are paid in cash directly to the driver ($2.50-$3.75 EC depending on distance); passengers flag buses down anywhere along the route. Ferry tickets to Nevis are bought in cash at the Basseterre Ferry Terminal ticket window before boarding.
transit.hours: Buses run roughly 5:30am-10pm with reduced evening and Sunday service; no fixed timetable since routes are flagged down. The Nevis ferry runs several scheduled sailings daily, with reduced service on weekends.
transit.note: Public buses cover Basseterre and villages around the island but do not serve Frigate Bay or the Southeast Peninsula resort areas; a taxi or rental car is needed for those.

train: St. Kitts Scenic Railway (tourist heritage train around the island)
bus: Private route buses/vans (green 'H' plates) from Basseterre to Sandy Point, Capesterre, St. Peter's, Molyneux, and Saddlers

transit.m: Taxi only, no public bus serves the airport (10 min)

tip.r: Restaurants often add a 10% service charge to the bill; if not already included, tipping about 10% is appreciated. Round up taxi fares.
